content:
Texas voters are turning out in record numbers. Fox News reported on October 22 that the state saw record-breaking turnout on the first day of early voting — and Webb County’s high-stakes races are right in the middle of the surge.

Early voting in Texas runs October 19 through October 30, with Election Day on Tuesday, November 3. Webb County voters have 14 early-voting locations, including the Webb County Elections Office at 720 Convent Ave. in Laredo. The county uses countywide vote centers, so on Election Day you may vote at any of the county’s polling locations.

What’s at stake in Webb County

This is not a quiet ballot. Webb County voters are choosing a new mayor of Laredo — incumbent Víctor Treviño faces challengers including Alfonso “Poncho” Casso, Jose “JD” Gonzalez, Alyssa Cigarroa, and Jorge Garza — plus city council seats, school board seats, and the marquee U.S. House race in Texas’s 28th District between Democratic incumbent Henry Cuellar and Republican challenger Tano Tijerina. The statewide ballot also features a U.S. Senate contest between James Talarico and Ken Paxton.

Deadlines that matter right now

  • Friday, October 23 (tomorrow): last day to apply for a ballot by mail — the application must be received at PO Box 233, not merely postmarked.
  • Friday, October 30: last day of early voting.
  • Tuesday, November 3: Election Day. Mail ballots must be received at PO Box 233 and postmarked by Election Day, or hand-delivered by the voter by 7 p.m.

Bring an accepted form of photo ID to vote. Webb County’s day-by-day early-voting totals are being tracked as they come in — and with statewide turnout breaking records, the question for Webb County is whether the border’s voters show up in force or sit this one out. The offices on this ballot — mayor, council, Congress — decide water, roads, bridges, trade, and the cost of living here for years.

title: Texas Shatters Day-One Early Voting Record as Webb County's High-Stakes Races Hit the Final Stretch
